```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
# The taxadb code below is shown, not run: it needs the taxadb package and a
# network connection, and taxastand does not depend on taxadb. The results come
# from data-raw/taxadb-vignette.R, saved in inst/extdata/taxadb-example.rds.
ex <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "taxadb-example.rds", package = "taxastand"))
```

`taxastand` matches names against a reference table that you supply. It does not download one. The [taxadb](https://docs.ropensci.org/taxadb/) package fills that gap: it provides versioned snapshots of several standard taxonomic databases (ITIS, Catalog of Life, GBIF, NCBI and others) that you can query from R. This vignette shows how to take a table from taxadb and use it as a `taxastand` reference, using ITIS as the example.

The code that uses taxadb is shown but not run when this vignette is built, so that `taxastand` does not need to depend on taxadb. The results shown were made from the ITIS snapshot `r ex$snapshot` with taxadb `r ex$taxadb_version` (script: `data-raw/taxadb-vignette.R`).

## Get a table

Install taxadb, then ask for a provider's table in the Darwin Core (`dwc`) schema. The first call downloads the snapshot (a Parquet file) to a local directory; later calls reuse it. The table is a lazy database table, so filter it before collecting it into memory.

```r
library(taxadb)
library(dplyr)

available_versions()   # snapshots you can ask for
available_providers()  # databases and schemas

itis <- taxa_tbl(provider = "itis", schema = "dwc")
colnames(itis)
```

The columns `taxastand` uses are `taxonID`, `acceptedNameUsageID`, `taxonomicStatus` and `scientificName`. taxadb has all of them, with one catch: in taxadb the author is in a separate column, `scientificNameAuthorship`, but `taxastand` matches on the author and wants it as part of `scientificName`. So paste the two together.

## Make a reference

Whole databases are large (ITIS has about one million names), so take the part you need. Here, the ferns of one family:

```r
ref <- itis |>
  filter(family == "Polypodiaceae") |>
  collect() |>
  mutate(
    scientificName = ifelse(
      is.na(scientificNameAuthorship),
      scientificName,
      paste(scientificName, scientificNameAuthorship)
    )
  ) |>
  select(taxonID, acceptedNameUsageID, taxonomicStatus, scientificName)
```

The filter keeps accepted names and their synonyms, which is what resolving a name needs. The result has `r ex$n_names` names, in these statuses:

```{r status, echo = FALSE}
print(ex$status_counts, row.names = FALSE)
```

and the synonyms look like this (`acceptedNameUsageID` points to the accepted name):

```{r ref-head, echo = FALSE}
print(ex$reference_head, row.names = FALSE)
```

## Resolve names

From here it is the usual `taxastand` workflow. For a large reference, prepare it once with `ts_prepare_reference()` (see the "Large references" section of the [basics](basics.html) vignette).

```r
library(taxastand)

ref_prepared <- ts_prepare_reference(ref)

queries <- c(
  "Polypodium vulgare L.",
  "Phymatodes scolopendria (Burm. f.) Ching",
  "Microsorum scolopendria",
  "Pleopeltis polylepis var. erythrolepis (Weath.) T. Wendt",
  "Polypodium pelucidum Kaulf."
)

ts_resolve_names(queries, ref_prepared, match_no_auth = TRUE)
```

```{r resolved, echo = FALSE}
print(ex$resolved[, c("resolved_name", "matched_status", "match_type")], row.names = FALSE)
```

The rows are in the order of the queries. The first and fourth queries are accepted names that match exactly, and the fifth matches an accepted name after a spelling correction (`auto_fuzzy`). *Phymatodes scolopendria* (second) is an ITIS synonym, so it resolves to the accepted *Microsorum scolopendria*. The third query has no author, so it matched by ignoring the author (`auto_noauth`, which `match_no_auth = TRUE` allows).

Names above species rank (a genus such as *Polypodium* L.) are not matched by `taxastand`, and `ts_resolve_names()` warns that they are left out of the results. They are fine to leave in the reference.

## Other databases

The same steps work for other taxadb providers: change `provider` and filter on the columns that provider has. Check `colnames()` first, since the columns differ between databases.

| Provider | `provider =` | Notes |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Catalog of Life | `"col"` | Broad coverage, all kingdoms |
| GBIF backbone | `"gbif"` | Includes many names of uncertain status |
| ITIS | `"itis"` | Mostly North American taxa |
| NCBI | `"ncbi"` | Names of organisms in sequence databases |
| Open Tree of Life | `"ott"` | Names in the synthetic tree |

Check each provider's licence before reusing a table. The `"fb"` (FishBase) and `"slb"` (SeaLifeBase) tables, for example, are CC BY-NC.

## Reproducibility

taxadb snapshots are versioned. Pass `version =` to `taxa_tbl()` (see `available_versions()`) and record it with your results, so that the reference is the same the next time you run the analysis. Cite both the provider and taxadb.
